question: A compliance officer must update an internal policy to reflect a new regulation. Which sequence of stages should she work through?
options: A) Pull the obligations out of the current policy; list what the regulation now requires; mark the clauses affected; draft the replacement wording.
B) Mark the clauses affected; draft the replacement wording; pull the obligations out of the current policy; list what the regulation now requires.
C) List what the regulation now requires; draft the replacement wording; pull the obligations out of the current policy; mark the clauses affected.
D) Draft the replacement wording; list what the regulation now requires; mark the clauses affected; pull the obligations out of the current policy.
correct_answers: A) Pull the obligations out of the current policy; list what the regulation now requires; mark the clauses affected; draft the replacement wording.
explanations: Correct. Establishing what the policy says today and what the regulation now demands gives the two lists that make a gap visible, the affected clauses fall out of that comparison, and only then is there something specific to redraft.
Clauses cannot be marked as affected until both the existing obligations and the new requirements have been set out to compare.
Drafting immediately after reading the regulation ignores what the policy already covers, so it produces new text that duplicates or contradicts existing clauses.
Replacement wording written before either the current position or the new requirement is known has nothing to replace and nothing to satisfy.
